text:
Liam H: Quick follow-up from the autoscale sync — I sketched an adaptive policy that mixes short-term reactive bursts with a small predictive headroom buffer. Wanted to surface tradeoffs and get 👀 before I draft an RFC.

Anika S: pinged the thread — looks interesting. can you summarise the admission path? reactive vs predictive in a sentence?

Liam H: Sure — reactive handles current queue depth (scale-out asap), predictive injects a tiny headroom token allowance sized by recent peak qps to reduce churn + prewarm calls. Reactive is low-cost but noisy; predictive reduces cold-starts at modest reserved GPU cost.

Raj P: How do you size "tiny" headroom? curious about multi-tenant fairness. we don't want big tenants hogging burst credits.

Liam H: Proposal: per-tenant headroom = max(2 slots, min(10% of tenant steady-state tokens, 8 slots)). Also keep a global burst pool for unallocated short spikes. Headroom decays over 5m if unused.

Morgan C: That decay window seems long — 5m might hold GPUs idle for longer than we want at high cost. Could we use adaptive decay based on cluster utilization? e.g., shorter when avg util > 70%.

Liam H: Yep, planned: decay halved if cluster_util > target_util (default 70%). So in tight clusters headroom evaporates faster.

Anika S: Admission control: do we evict or queue when admission fails? we need consistent SLOs for Dedicated customers.

Raj P: For Dedicated we should prefer queuing (backpressure) over eviction for higher tier tenants. Preemptible workloads can be evicted. That suggests tenant QoS classes + fallback policies.

Liam H: Agreed. Policy matrix draft: 
- Tier=Enterprise: queue + can request burst from global pool (billing event)
- Tier=Standard: queue with soft timeout, fallback to hosted model variant (smaller)
- Tier=Preemptible: best-effort, eviction allowed

ops-bot: Note: new ticket created: INF-5123 "policy: adaptive headroom + tiered admission"

Morgan C: How do we implement the global burst pool without a central bottleneck? current operator tries to be stateless-ish.

Liam H: Implementation idea: lease tokens via the Operator API — small CRD that contains ephemeral counters. Operators are authoritative per-shard; a lightweight distributed counter uses CRD CAS with backoff. Keep counters coarse-grained (per-region, not per-node) to reduce churn.

Anika S: CRD CAS is fine but watch for apiserver pressure at scale. Maybe use a sidecar-based local cache with probabilistic reconciliation to apiserver (sync every 5s) and accept rare transient oversubscribe with safety bounds.

Raj P: Also need a clear failure mode: if operator loses connection to control-plane, tenants in prewarm should fallback to reactive admission (no headroom) and signal + alert. We should avoid silent degradation.

Liam H: Good call — add explicit healthcheck state and signal to Console (metric + alert) when headroom is disabled for >30s.

Morgan C: What about the model variant fallback? do we allow automatic downscaling of sequence length or quantization level? that seems risky for quality.

Anika S: We should expose a policy knob per route: allowed_fallbacks = [variant-small, quantized-8bit] and a quality budget token. Ops can set policy per-customer. Default: only fallback to smaller model if response latency SLO is at risk for >3s.

Liam H: Example config snippet I prototyped:
```yaml
policy_name: adaptive-headroom-v1
headroom:
  base_slots: 2
  pct_of_steady: 0.10
  max_slots: 8
  decay_secs: 300
admission:
  tiers:
    enterprise: { action: queue, allow_global_burst: true }
    standard: { action: queue, soft_timeout: 45, fallback: [model-small] }
    preemptible: { action: best_effort, allow_eviction: true }
```

Raj P: Nice. For telemetry we need per-tenant metrics: headroom_allocated, headroom_used, headroom_reclaimed, admission_rejections, fallback_invocations. Also histograms for queue latency.

Liam H: Will add to RFC. Action items: (1) I'll draft RFC with config schema + operator shim sketch, (2) Morgan to prototype lease CRD perf tests, (3) Anika to review fallback QoS semantics.

Anika S: I can take (3). Also request we add an explicit billing event design if we allow charged bursts. Need PM input.

Morgan C: Starting perf harness next week. I'll try CRD CAS vs sidecar cache and report perf/etcd qps numbers.

Liam H: Thanks — I'll post RFC link here when ready. For now, small poll: thumbs if you agree to the hybrid approach (reactive + small predictive headroom).

Raj P: :+1:

Anika S: :+1:

Morgan C: :+1:

Liam H: :thumbsup: great, will follow up with RFC.
